messages:
maya (Sales): Hey team — Customer asked for exact language for encryption/KMS in the vendor risk questionnaire. Can we give a concise answer they can paste into the SIG/CAIQ? They specifically asked about at-rest, in-transit, BYOK/HSM options, and rotation.
li (Solutions Eng): Quick draft below — feel free to edit for legal tone. Short summary first then a one-paragraph detail:
li (Solutions Eng): Summary: All customer data is encrypted in-transit (TLS 1.3) and at-rest (AES-256). We support customer-managed keys (BYOK) via major KMS providers (AWS KMS, GCP KMS, Azure Key Vault) and can integrate with HSM-backed keys for Private deployments. We use envelope encryption; platform never stores plaintext CMKs.
asha (Security): Add: We log all key access and key-wrapping operations to immutable audit trails (retention per contract). FIPS 140-2/140-3 attestation is available via the customer HSM provider when BYOK is used. For hosted customers, the default KMS is provider-managed; for enterprise we recommend Dedicated or Private so keys remain under customer control. :white_check_mark:
li (Solutions Eng): More detail for SIG/CAIQ item answers (single-paragraph form): "Redwood Inference enforces TLS 1.3 for all in-transit traffic. At-rest data is encrypted using AES-256-GCM; we implement envelope encryption where data encryption keys (DEKs) are encrypted with customer-managed master keys (CMKs). Customers may provide CMKs via supported cloud KMS (ARNs / resource IDs) or enable BYOK in Private deployments. For HSM-backed keys, we support integration with customer HSMs (via vendor APIs or KMIP) for on-prem/private deployments; HSM attestations (FIPS 140-2/3) are provided by the HSM vendor. Key rotation can be automated by the customer or configured to follow a rotation policy; Redwood does not retain plaintext keys and only stores wrapped CMKs. Access to key operations is logged and available in audit exports for compliance reviews." 
li (Solutions Eng): Example config snippet we give in POC docs (pasteable):
li (Solutions Eng): ```
{
  "key_provider": "aws-kms",
  "key_id": "arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/abcd-ef01-2345-6789",
  "rotation": "customer-managed",
  "mode": "envelope"
}
```
li (Solutions Eng): Note: that's illustrative only — actual fields vary by deployment.
jon (Prospect IT): Can you confirm: do you ever export customer keys out of our account? We need to be explicit for procurement.
asha (Security): No. If you provide a customer-managed CMK in your cloud account, we do not export the CMK. For hosted customers using Redwood-managed KMS, Redwood manages the CMK in our provider account per contract; for Dedicated/Private the CMKs remain in customer control. We only store encrypted/wrapped key materials and never persist plaintext DEKs or master key material.
maya (Sales): Customer also asked about rotation cadence requirements and whether we support automatic rotation (90/180/365 days) and forced rotation in an incident.
li (Solutions Eng): We support both. Typical options:
- Customer-managed rotation: you rotate in your KMS and update the CMK reference (no downtime if you follow typical re-wrap best practices).
- Redwood-managed rotation: we can rotate DEKs and rewrap with the CMK on a schedule (configurable by contract), defaulting to 90 days for high-security customers. Forced rotation (emergency rewrap) supported via SRE runbook; will trigger a rolling re-encryption with coordination.
asha (Security): For SIG/CAIQ and vendor review language, here's a one-line: "Redwood supports tenant isolation of key material and BYOK/HSM integrations; key usage and admin operations are logged and available for audit." 
jon (Prospect IT): What about bring-your-own-HSM (not just KMS backed by HSM) — we need attestable HSM with L3. We have a compliance requirement for HSM with attestation.
li (Solutions Eng): For Private deployments we can integrate with customer HSM appliances or external HSM clusters via KMIP/PKCS11 depending on vendor. Attestation and FIPS level come from the HSM vendor — we can include vendor-signed attestation documents in the compliance pack. Typical POC timeline for HSM integration: 2–3 weeks to wire up network and key sync for a single environment, plus validation.
maya (Sales): Are we safe to say: "supports HSM-backed CMKs via customer-provided HSMs for Private deployments"?
asha (Security): Yes, with this caveat: include that attestation documents are provided by the HSM vendor and that network/access controls must be configured by the customer. Also note: Redwood does not perform HSM key generation on behalf of the customer unless explicitly contracted and audited.
deploy-bot: Notice: pre-sales template updated -> https://redwood.internal/sales/presales-crypto-template (edit history available)
maya (Sales): Thanks — I'll send this back to procurement with the short SIG-ready paragraph and attach the attestation caveats. Action: li to add the example snippet to the POC repo; asha to attach standard audit language and attestation checklist. :pray:
li (Solutions Eng): Will do, I already opened PR to presales repo.
asha (Security): I'll bundle the standard attestation text and sample SOC2/KMS audit excerpts in the compliance pack.
jon (Prospect IT): Great, that should cover it. Will loop legal. Thanks all. :+1:
